title: Longest Unequal Adjacent Groups Subsequence I
statement:
You get a string array `words` and an array `groups` of the same length `n`, where every `groups[i]` is 0 or 1 and labels `words[i]`. All strings in `words` are different.

Choose a subsequence of `words` (some of its positions, kept in their original order) in which every two neighbouring chosen words carry different labels in `groups`, so the labels alternate between 0 and 1. Make it as long as possible and return the chosen words in order. If several longest choices exist, any one of them is accepted.
constraints: All strings in words are distinct
words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Look at `groups` as runs of equal labels, such as `1 1 | 0 0 0 | 1`. An alternating subsequence can take at most one word from each run, because two words of the same run have the same label and every word between them does too. Taking exactly one word from every run is always possible, so the answer's length is the number of runs. A simple greedy builds it: keep the first word, then keep any word whose label differs from the last kept one. (A slower O(n²) DP over "longest alternating subsequence ending at i" gives the same length.)

## Approach

1. Start `result` with `words[0]` and remember its label in `lastGroup`.
2. Walk `i` from 1 to the end.
3. When `groups[i]` differs from `lastGroup`, a new run begins: append `words[i]` and update `lastGroup`.
4. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`words = ["e", "a", "b"]`, `groups = [0, 0, 1]`. Start with `result = ["e"]`, `lastGroup = 0`. At `i = 1` the label is 0, the same, so `"a"` is skipped. At `i = 2` the label is 1, so `"b"` is appended and `lastGroup` becomes 1. The answer is `["e", "b"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the arrays.
- Space: O(n) for the returned list; O(1) besides it.

## Pitfalls

- Return the words, not their indices or labels.
- Skipping a word whose label matches never hurts: it belongs to the same run as the word already kept, so taking it could not add length.
- Do not reset `lastGroup` on skipped words; only a kept word changes it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | the alternating subsequence built so far |
| `lastGroup` | label of the most recently kept word |
| `i` | index of the word being considered |

narration.2: The first word always starts a longest answer, so keep it.
narration.3: Remember the label of the last word kept.
narration.5: Look at every later word in order.
narration.6: A different label means a new run of equal labels starts here.
narration.7: Take this word: it keeps the labels alternating.
narration.8: Its label is now the one the next kept word must differ from.
narration.11: One word from each run is the longest possible alternating subsequence.
